title: Client consultation, product records and the reaction record
audience: Makeup artists and makeup businesses that take client bookings and keep records of the products used on each client
learningOutcomes: Run a consultation that captures a client's allergies, previous reactions and skin conditions that need referral
Record each product used on a client, with the information needed to trace a reaction
Complete a reaction record and refer the client where needed
referencesAtStart: Official references for this lesson: this lesson draws on the product and allergy sources used in NEW-MUA-02, NEW-MUA-03 and NEW-MUA-04. Record-keeping periods for makeup businesses were not confirmed for any state in this draft.

instruction.heading: The consultation before the first appointment
instruction.body: A consultation before the first appointment gives the artist the information needed to choose safe products. The artist asks about known allergies to cosmetics, fragrances or any ingredient, previous reactions to makeup or skin products, and any skin condition the client has, such as a current rash, broken skin or a condition the client's doctor is treating. Where a client reports a condition that needs medical advice, the artist does not offer a view on it, and suggests the client speaks to a health professional before the appointment. The answers are recorded on the client's file, dated, and checked again before each appointment.

instruction.heading: Recording each product used
instruction.body: For each appointment, the artist records the products used on the client. The record gives the product name, the brand, the batch or lot number if the product has one, the date of the appointment, and the area of use. A product that was patch tested is recorded with the test date and result, as set out in the preventive test lesson. A record that names only the kit, such as eye look or bridal palette, does not allow a reaction to be traced to a product, so the individual products must be listed. The product record is kept with the client's file, and is available if the client later reports a reaction.

instruction.heading: The reaction record
instruction.body: When a client reports a reaction, the artist records what the client reported, the product or products involved, the batch if known, the time of the reaction, the action taken and the referral given. The product is withdrawn from use for that client, and the artist does not apply it again. The record is written at the time of the event, or as soon as possible after it, and it is signed or initialled by the artist. A reaction record is not a diagnosis. The artist records what was observed and reported, and the client's health professional makes any diagnosis.

instruction.heading: Keeping records and the open questions
instruction.body: The business keeps client records in a way that can be found and used if a reaction is reported later. The period for which these records must be kept, and any privacy rules that apply to them, depend on the state or territory and on the business's own policy. Neither was confirmed for this draft. UNCONFIRMED: the retention period and the privacy requirements for client records of this kind. A reviewer must confirm them before the lesson is approved.

procedure: Complete the client consultation on allergies, previous reactions and skin conditions before the first appointment
Refer the client to a health professional where a condition needs medical advice, and record the referral
Check the consultation answers again at the start of each appointment
Record each product used on the client, by product name, brand, batch if available, date and area of use
Record the patch test date and result for any product that was tested
If a reaction is reported, withdraw the product for that client, complete the reaction record, and refer the client where needed

workedExamples.situation: A client books a bridal makeup session. At the consultation she mentions a previous reaction to a fragrance in a cream she bought from a shop.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the artist record, and which products can be used?
workedExamples.reasoning: The artist records the reported fragrance reaction on the client's file, with the date and the product name if the client knows it. The artist then checks each product for fragrance, using the ingredient list and the safety data sheet, and does not use any product that contains fragrance for this client. The artist runs a preventive test on each new product before the appointment and records the results.

workedExamples.situation: On the day of an event, a client reports itching and redness on the cheek an hour after a foundation was applied.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the artist's record and referral step?
workedExamples.reasoning: The artist stops using the foundation for this client, and removes it from the skin in line with the product's own instructions. The reaction record notes the time, the product name, the batch if known, and the action taken. The artist refers the client to a health professional, and does not recommend a treatment. The reaction is recorded even though the event is outside the appointment.

equipmentAndPpe: Consultation form covering allergies, previous reactions and skin conditions
Product record for each appointment, listing each product by name and batch where available
Reaction record form, kept with the client's file

commonErrors.error: Recording only the kit name, so a product cannot be traced if a reaction is reported.
commonErrors.prevention: List each product used on the client, by name, batch if available, date and area.

commonErrors.error: Reusing a consultation answer from a client's first booking without checking it again.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the consultation at the start of every appointment, and update it if the client's answers have changed.

commonErrors.error: Continuing to use a product for a client after a reaction, because the client says it is mild.
commonErrors.prevention: Withdraw the product for that client, complete the reaction record and refer the client where needed.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson does not give medical advice, does not diagnose allergy or skin conditions, and does not give authority to treat a reaction. A client with a reaction is referred to a health professional.
UNCONFIRMED: the retention period and privacy requirements for client records of makeup services in any state or territory. A reviewer must confirm them before this lesson is approved.

qualityStandard: Each client's consultation answers are recorded before the first appointment and checked before each later one
Each product used on a client is recorded by name, date and area of use
Each reported reaction has a reaction record, and the product is withdrawn for that client
documentationEvidence: Dated consultation record for each client, with allergies, previous reactions and referrals
Product record for each appointment, listing the products used by name and area
Reaction record for each reported reaction, with the action taken and the referral
summary: A consultation records allergies, previous reactions and skin conditions that need referral
Each product used is recorded by name, batch if available, date and area, so a reaction can be traced
A reported reaction is recorded, the product is withdrawn for that client, and the client is referred
Retention and privacy rules for client records are UNCONFIRMED in this draft

knowledgeChecks.question: Which product record lets a reaction be traced to the product that caused it?
options: A note that the client had the bridal kit
A record of each product used by name, batch if available, date and area
A verbal account from the client after the appointment

knowledgeChecks.question: A client reports a reaction during an appointment. What is the first action?
options: Apply the same product again to see whether it recurs
Wait until the next appointment to mention it
Withdraw the product for that client and complete the reaction record

knowledgeChecks.question: What should the artist do with a client's skin condition that needs medical advice?
options: Suggest the client speaks to a health professional, and record the referral
Recommend a cream that will treat it before the appointment
Apply a makeup layer over the area to hide it
